# glinet_local_access (Resource)

Manages the access to the router from the LAN: the ports of the web UI, LuCI and SSH, the redirect to HTTPS and the session timeout of the web UI (`local-access.set_config` in the router API). The router has one local access configuration, so use one instance of this resource.

~> **Warning:** this resource can cut the access to the router, also the access of the provider. The web UI and the API that the provider uses have the same address. A change of `http_port`, `https_port` or `redirect_https_enabled` moves this address: after the apply, change `host` of the provider to the new address, for example `http://192.168.8.1:8080`, or the next plan cannot read the router. After such a write, the provider saves the written values in the state before it reads the router again, and shows a warning; when that read fails or gets no answer within 5 seconds, the apply does not fail. It is not known whether the router answers the write before it moves the address; when it does not answer, the apply fails and the write was possibly done. A change of `ssh_enabled` or `ssh_port` can end the SSH access to the router.

Each write sends all attributes, as the web UI does, also the LuCI attributes when LuCI is not installed. When an attribute is not set, the provider sends back the router value that it reads just before the write. The five ports must all be different; the provider checks this before the write, also against the router values of the ports that are not set. The router refuses a port that is in use and SSH with a weak admin password. The write of this resource was not tested on a router; the parameters come from the router's web UI. Destroy removes the resource from the Terraform state and does not change the router.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A change of http_port, https_port or redirect_https_enabled moves the router API.
# After the apply, change the host of the provider to the new address.
resource "glinet_local_access" "this" {
  session_timeout = 1800
  ssh_enabled     = true
  ssh_port        = 2222
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `http_port` (Number) Port of the web UI and the API over HTTP (`http_port` in the router API). From 1 to 65535, and not a port that browsers block, for example 22, 25 or 6000 (the bad ports of the Fetch standard), as the web UI permits. When it is not set, the router value does not change.
- `https_port` (Number) Port of the web UI and the API over HTTPS (`https_port` in the router API). From 1 to 65535, and not a port that browsers block, for example 22, 25 or 6000 (the bad ports of the Fetch standard), as the web UI permits. When it is not set, the router value does not change.
- `luci_http_port` (Number) Port of LuCI over HTTP (`luci_http_port` in the router API). The web UI shows it only when LuCI is installed. From 1 to 65535, and not a port that browsers block, for example 22, 25 or 6000 (the bad ports of the Fetch standard), as the web UI permits. When it is not set, the router value does not change.
- `luci_https_port` (Number) Port of LuCI over HTTPS (`luci_https_port` in the router API). The web UI shows it only when LuCI is installed. From 1 to 65535, and not a port that browsers block, for example 22, 25 or 6000 (the bad ports of the Fetch standard), as the web UI permits. When it is not set, the router value does not change.
- `luci_redirect_https_enabled` (Boolean) Whether the router redirects HTTP to HTTPS for LuCI (`luci_redirect_https` in the router API). The web UI shows it only when LuCI is installed. When it is not set, the router value does not change.
- `redirect_https_enabled` (Boolean) Whether the router redirects HTTP to HTTPS for the web UI (`redirect_https` in the router API). What the redirect does to the API calls of the provider over HTTP is not known; use a `host` with `https://` when it is `true`. When it is not set, the router value does not change.
- `session_timeout` (Number) Session timeout of the web UI in seconds, from 60 to 10800 in steps of 60 (`session_timeout` in the router API). The web UI shows it in minutes. When it is not set, the router value does not change.
- `ssh_enabled` (Boolean) Whether the SSH server of the router is enabled (`ssh_enabled` in the router API). The router refuses `true` when the admin password is too weak. When it is not set, the router value does not change. Firmware 4.7.0 does not return `ssh_enabled`: with such firmware the provider reads null, and a write sends no `ssh_enabled` when it is not set. When it is set and the router does not return `ssh_enabled` in the read before the write, the apply fails before the write.
- `ssh_port` (Number) Port of the SSH server (`ssh_port` in the router API), from 1 to 65535. When it is not set, the router value does not change.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Always `local_access`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# The import ID is always "local_access".
terraform import glinet_local_access.this local_access
```
